scopeNote: The 16 files named by the unit plus dropdown-integration.tsx (same directory, same public API). The namespace has 21 downstream registry items; the two consumers outside the directory (application/table table.tsx TableRowActionsDropdown, application/app-navigation header-navigation.tsx which imports DropdownAccountButton) compile against the unchanged namespace and were verified against it by typecheck.

semanticDifferences: Base UI splits React Aria's single `MenuItem` into one part per behaviour (Item/RadioItem/CheckboxItem/LinkItem/SubmenuTrigger). `Dropdown.Item` picks the part from the consumer props: a submenu trigger context, `href`, then the collection's resolved selection mode.

React Aria kept selection on the collection (`selectedKeys`/`onSelectionChange` at Menu and Section level); Base UI has a `RadioGroup`+`RadioItem` pair for single selection and independent `CheckboxItem`s for multiple. A selection-owner context in dropdown.tsx keeps the React Aria props as the public API and derives the per-item part from them; sections that declare `selectionMode` own their state exactly as React Aria's `GroupSelectionManager` did, sections that do not share the menu's selection.

`CheckboxItem`/`RadioItem` default `closeOnClick` to false, React Aria closes a single-select menu on selection, so `closeOnClick` is passed explicitly (true for single, false for multiple, true for plain items) to keep the close behaviour identical.
Base UI has no `onAction`; item activation is `onClick`. `onAction`/`onPress`/`onClick` are all accepted and invoked from one handler.

`isDisabled` maps to Base UI's `disabled`; Base UI emits only `data-disabled`, so `aria-disabled="true"` is added explicitly to keep React Aria's a11y surface. Base UI's roving focus still lands on a disabled item (it cannot be activated: Enter/click are ignored), whereas React Aria skipped it — the highlight styling is suppressed for disabled items so the visual result matches the baseline.

React Aria's typeahead text override is `textValue`, Base UI's is `label`: `textValue ?? label` is passed so typeahead matches the same strings (verified: `Dropdown.Menu`/items in every demo keep their text overrides).

The menu role lives on the menu box inside Base UI's popup, not on the popup: Base UI's popup also contains the content a consumer renders beside the menu (search fields, footers) and axe flags non-menu children of `role="menu"`. `Dropdown.Popover` therefore clears the popup's own role/aria-labelledby and `Dropdown.Menu` renders `role="menu"` + `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` (defaulting to the trigger id, which `Dropdown.Root` generates and passes to the trigger) — the DOM React Aria produced.

Base UI's popup keeps `data-open`/`data-ending-style` for the whole enter/exit phase (`data-starting-style` lasts a frame), which is what React Aria's `data-entering`/`data-exiting` meant; the popover's animation classes are driven from the popup state instead of render props.

Submenus are explicit parts: `Dropdown.Submenu` = `Menu.SubmenuRoot` and the `Dropdown.Item` it wraps renders `Menu.SubmenuTrigger` (delay/closeDelay forwarded, React Aria's 200 ms hover delay is the default). A submenu trigger cannot also be a checkbox/radio item in Base UI: such an item keeps its selection *state* (indicator shows React Aria's `isSelected && hasSubmenu` = indeterminate) but only opens the submenu, and it carries `role="menuitem"` without `aria-checked` (React Aria announced it as a checked menuitemcheckbox).

React Aria's `MenuTrigger trigger="contextMenu"` opens on right click and anchors the popover at the pointer position (react-aria stores the press point as a virtual element). Base UI's `ContextMenu.Root` also anchors at the pointer by default, so the recorded geometry is unchanged; `placement` still maps to side/align and the context-menu default `align: 'start'` matches React Aria's removed aria-haspopup/aria-expanded behaviour.

Base UI's context menu Trigger renders an area and emits data-popup-open/data-pressed, and — like React Aria's context-menu trigger — adds no aria-haspopup/aria-expanded (verified on the migrated trigger).

Only the filter matcher is reused: Base UI's `Autocomplete` is a full combobox with its own Portal/Positioner/Popup, no selection state and `Autocomplete.Item` rows, so it cannot replace a checkbox menu that already lives inside the dropdown's popup. The two search demos therefore keep `Dropdown.Menu` and filter their items locally with Base UI's filter (`Autocomplete.useFilter()` = the same `Intl.Collator` matcher React Aria's `useFilter` used, `contains` with the same base sensitivity).

Matching runs against each item's `textValue` (as React Aria's collection filter did) so typed queries select the same rows — including dropdown-search-advanced's upstream textValue/label mismatch, which is preserved.

React Aria's Autocomplete also moved focus from the search field into the filtered list with ArrowDown and cleared the query on Escape before closing; both are reproduced in the two files (verified in a browser).

migrationRecord.publicComponent: Dropdown (Root, Popover, Menu, Section, SectionHeader, Item, Separator, DotsButton) + Dropdown.Submenu
migrationRecord.existingUntitledUiBehavior: Dropdown.Root was React Aria's MenuTrigger: the first child is the trigger element (a Button, a DotsButton or a raw AriaButton) and the second is the overlay; `trigger="contextMenu"` opened it on right click. Dropdown.Popover was an AriaPopover defaulting to `placement="bottom right"` with the popover box styling and the enter/exit animations. Dropdown.Menu was an AriaMenu wrapping a role=menu box inside that popover, owning selectionMode/selectedKeys/onSelectionChange; Dropdown.Section was an AriaMenuSection with the same selection props plus a Header; Dropdown.Item was an AriaMenuItem with label/addon/icon/avatarUrl/unstyled/selectionIndicator props and render-prop className/children; Dropdown.Separator was an AriaSeparator; Dropdown.DotsButton was an AriaButton with an aria-label and state-driven hover/pressed/focus classes. Submenus used React Aria's SubmenuTrigger around an Item + Popover.
migrationRecord.canonicalBehavioralContract: A trigger element that opens a portaled menu on press (or on right click for the context-menu flavour); the menu carries role=menu, is named by the trigger (or its own aria-label) and holds items with role menuitem/menuitemradio/menuitemcheckbox; keyboard: first item focused on open, ArrowUp/ArrowDown roving highlight, Home/End, typeahead, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; submenus open on hover/ArrowRight with their own menu, and Escape closes only the child menu; selection is controlled either by the menu or by a section (single => radio semantics + close on select, multiple => checkbox semantics + stay open); the popover is placement-driven, portaled, animated on enter and exit, and content rendered beside the menu (search fields, footers) stays inside the popover.
migrationRecord.baseUiCompositionChosen: Dropdown.Root = Menu.Root (or ContextMenu.Root for trigger="contextMenu") with the first child rendered through Trigger's `render` prop; Dropdown.Popover = Menu.Portal > Menu.Positioner (side/align/sideOffset/alignOffset/collisionPadding/collisionAvoidance from the React Aria placement/offset/crossOffset/containerPadding/shouldFlip props) > Menu.Popup (the popover box, role cleared); Dropdown.Menu = the role=menu box with the selection context, wrapping its items in Menu.RadioGroup when the menu itself is single-select; Dropdown.Section = Menu.Group, or Menu.RadioGroup when the section declares selectionMode="single"; Dropdown.SectionHeader = Menu.GroupLabel; Dropdown.Item = Menu.Item | Menu.RadioItem | Menu.CheckboxItem | Menu.LinkItem | Menu.SubmenuTrigger chosen from props/context; Dropdown.Separator = Menu.Separator; Dropdown.Submenu = Menu.SubmenuRoot; Dropdown.DotsButton = a native button composed as the trigger.
migrationRecord.whyNotOneToOne: React Aria's trigger/popover/menu triple must be unrolled into Base UI's explicit parts (Root + Trigger + Portal/Positioner/Popup), and React Aria's single MenuItem + collection-level selection state has to be re-expressed as five Base UI item parts plus a RadioGroup/CheckboxItem split, which is why dropdown.tsx carries a selection-owner context rather than a 1:1 prop map. The popover box and the menu box also had to stay two elements (the payload stacks backgrounds on both, e.g. dropdown-account-button's bg-secondary_alt popover around a bg-primary menu) while Base UI merges the menu role into its popup — hence the role is moved onto the menu box.

publicApiChanges.after: Dropdown.Submenu takes the same two children (the trigger `Dropdown.Item` first, then its `Dropdown.Popover`) and forwards delay/closeDelay/isOpen/defaultOpen/onOpenChange
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI nests submenus through explicit SubmenuRoot/SubmenuTrigger parts and the React Aria import had to go.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Additive; consumers that compose their own submenu can use it with the same child shape they used for React Aria's SubmenuTrigger.

publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI's parts type their own DOM surface; the unused React Aria event set was dropped rather than re-declared.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Every prop any in-repo call site passes is declared (verified by typecheck across the 16 files plus the two consumers outside the directory). `onHoverStart`/`onFocusChange`-style hooks are gone; no call site used them.

publicApiChanges.before: { isSelected, isDisabled, isPressed, isFocused, isFocusVisible, hasSubmenu, isOpen, selectionMode }
publicApiChanges.after: same shape; `isPressed` is always false (Base UI exposes no item press state) and `isFocusVisible` is always false (Base UI focuses the item element itself)
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI's item state is {disabled, highlighted(, checked, open)}.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Both fields are kept for type compatibility; CSS should use `:focus-visible` on the item and `:active`-style hooks instead (the family's own markup does). The live fields — isSelected, isDisabled, isFocused, hasSubmenu, isOpen, selectionMode — are all accurate.

publicApiChanges.after: unchanged (the function form is still supported)
publicApiChanges.reason: React Aria exposed those states as render props; the states are now tracked from pointer/keyboard/focus events on the button.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Verified in a browser: the dots button reports hovered/pressed/focus-visible as before (the classes it derives from them are unchanged), and Base UI adds data-popup-open/data-pressed to the element for CSS consumers.

publicApiChanges.before: React Aria placement strings, defaults to "bottom right", physical left/right for sides and alignments
publicApiChanges.after: same strings and default; `start`/`end` map to Base UI's logical inline sides, and the alignment tokens left/right map to Base UI's start/end
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI positions with side+align and has no physical alignment tokens.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Side mapping keeps physical left/right (left => side left, right => side right); only the cross-axis alignment follows the logical edge Base UI supports, i.e. `left`/`right` align behave as start/end in RTL instead of physical edges — no in-repo call site depends on RTL physical alignment.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: behaviour change for RTL physical alignment only

stateSelectorChanges.from: placement-right|placement-top|placement-bottom:* (popover enter/exit slide, React Aria's Tailwind variants)
stateSelectorChanges.to: computed slide-in-from-* / slide-out-to-* classes selected from the resolved side (SLIDE_IN_BY_SIDE/SLIDE_OUT_BY_SIDE) inside the popup's className function
stateSelectorChanges.reason: Base UI emits data-side (not data-placement), and the React Aria variant plugin's placement-* variants only match data-placement. The className function already receives the popup state, so the slide is chosen from the same side token the Positioner is given (including inline-start/inline-end).

stateSelectorChanges.from: state.isEntering && 'duration-150 ease-out animate-in fade-in' / state.isExiting && 'duration-100 ease-in animate-out fade-out'
stateSelectorChanges.reason: React Aria kept data-entering for the whole enter animation; Base UI's data-starting-style exists for a single frame, so the enter animation hangs off data-open (present for the whole open phase) and the exit off data-ending-style (present until the popup unmounts). Measured: enter animation 'enter' runs on open, exit unmounts 123 ms (Escape) / 159 ms (trigger click) after close.
Base UI sets --transform-origin on the Positioner (the custom property inherits into the popup). Only affects scale/rotate animations; the dropdown popovers use fade+slide.
Base UI emits data-disabled on the item element itself.

Base UI sets data-highlighted on the item element for both hover (highlightItemOnHover defaults true) and keyboard navigation, so one ancestor-attribute variant replaces the hover/focus pair; the inner box is the styled element, hence `in-`. Verified in a browser: highlighted items get oklch(0.985 0 none), a hovered disabled item keeps a transparent background.
Base UI moves real DOM focus onto the item element, so :focus-visible on that element is the live signal and the styled box is its child.
Same highlight state, read from the item ancestor.

stateSelectorChanges.from: trigger render-prop classNames: ({isPressed, isFocusVisible}) / ({isPressed, isFocused}) => ... outline-2
stateSelectorChanges.to: 'active:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-2' (focus-visible flavour) or 'active:outline-2 focus:outline-2' (focused flavour) on the native trigger buttons
stateSelectorChanges.reason: The React Aria Button instances used as triggers became native buttons composed through Base UI's trigger `render` prop; the plugin's active/focus/focus-visible variants fall back to the native pseudo-classes on elements without data-rac, which is what React Aria's isPressed/isFocusVisible/isFocused meant.

stateSelectorChanges.to: unchanged class logic, driven by tracked isHovered/isPressed/isFocusVisible state + data-popup-open (Base UI adds it while the menu is open)
stateSelectorChanges.reason: The dots button is the trigger element, so its state arrives as DOM events rather than render props; the consumer-facing className function still receives the same state object.

stateSelectorChanges.from: (no RAC variant was dead in these files — all item state came from render props; the audit's placement-* entries were the only class-level variants)
stateSelectorChanges.reason: Recorded for the phase-7 audit: dropdown.tsx no longer contains any placement-*/selected:/open:/expanded: variant; the family's only attribute variants are Base UI's own (data-disabled, in-data-highlighted, in-focus-visible, data-popup-open).

The family renders ../avatar, ../checkbox (CheckboxBase), ../radio-buttons (RadioButtonBase) and ../toggle (ToggleBase) with their existing `isSelected`/`isIndeterminate` props; those primitives were not touched.

notes: node node_modules/typescript5/bin/tsc -p registry/untitledui/tsconfig.json -> 0 errors in the whole payload (including every consumer of the preserved API).

Browser verification through the real app (vite dev server, migration.html harness + catalog.html): harness dropdown case — trigger gets aria-haspopup="menu"/aria-expanded and an id, menu opens with role=menu, aria-label "Actions" and aria-labelledby=<trigger id>, first item focused, ArrowDown moves the highlight item by item, Escape closes (200 ms exit, unmounts at 123 ms) and returns focus to the trigger; zero console errors or warnings.

All 16 demos rendered, opened their menus and reported a named menu (sweep over catalog.html): account-breadcrumb (menuitemradio + aria-checked, selecting Sienna updates the trigger and closes the menu), account-button / account-card-* (groups + radiogroup sections + separators; Switch Account radios checked correctly; SectionHeader renders with the consumer's own classes and labels its group), avatar, button-simple/advanced (multiple selection toggles and keeps the menu open), button-link (single-select section with an array `selectedKeys`: choosing "Can view" updates the trigger label and closes), context-menu-simple/advanced (right click opens at the pointer: menu rect x/y == pointer x/y, side=bottom align=start), icon-simple/advanced, integration, search-simple/advanced (typing filters by textValue with the same `contains` semantics, selected rows stay checked, Escape clears the query without closing, ArrowDown moves focus into the list), nested submenus (2 and 3 levels deep) open on hover with side=right.

axe-core (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa) on the harness page with the menu open and on the catalog's selection menus: no new violations (only the pre-recorded slider `label`, nav-account-card `button-name`/`image-alt`, plus the catalog's avatar `image-alt` which comes from the untouched `alt={label}` expression that the React Aria build also rendered).

Documented gaps (not blockers): Base UI's roving focus still lands on a disabled item (it cannot be activated; highlight styling is suppressed for it), a submenu trigger is a plain menuitem without aria-checked, `isPressed`/`isFocusVisible` in the item render-prop state are inert, and `placement` alignment tokens are logical rather than physical in RTL.
